Member of Technical Staff - Applied Scientist I
Formal Methods for AI Driven Software Development Life Cycle

San Francisco Bay Area | Bellevue, Washington | Hybrid |

About AIVista

NTT DATA AIVista, Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of NTT DATA, is based in Silicon Valley. We develop AI products for enterprises operating in complex regulatory environments. We work with NTT DATA Inc., NTT DATA Japan, and NTT DOCOMO to deploy systems for NTT clients. Our clients combine AIVista's product AI expertise with NTT DATA's industry knowledge and systems-integration experience.

The Role

The Applied Scientist will develop methods that turn natural-language intent into structured, machine-checkable artifacts and use those artifacts to make AI-driven software development more verifiable, traceable, and reliable. You will work from policies, regulations, standard operating procedures, requirements, process descriptions, application programming interfaces, and code to construct formal specifications, rule ontologies, process ontologies, contracts, tests, and proofs with complete source traceability.

The work addresses two distinct assurance problems. Validation asks whether a formal artifact faithfully captures authorized intent. Verification asks whether an implementation satisfies that artifact. You will build measurable validation methods for omissions and mistranslations, integrate independent checkers and proof systems, and carry the resulting evidence through the AI-driven software development life cycle. The objective is a practical development workflow in which models may propose requirements, designs, code, tests, or proofs, while deterministic checkers, versioned evidence, and human authority determine what is accepted.

Responsibilities

 - Develop autoformalization methods that translate policies, procedures, regulations, requirements, and process descriptions into typed rules, process models, contracts, and formal specifications.

 - Design restricted domain-specific languages and formal semantics that domain experts and engineers can review together, with clause-level provenance and versioned change histories.

 - Build validation stacks using controlled source language, concretization, counterexamples, back-translation, cross-representation consistency, independent dual translation, and expert adjudication.

 - Create specification-mutation, non-vacuity, and seeded-defect benchmarks that measure detection rates for omissions, weakenings, exception errors, and mistranslations.

 - Integrate satisfiability modulo theories solvers, model checkers, theorem provers, static analyzers, type systems, and property-based or fuzz testing into independent verification harnesses.

 - Develop verifier-guided generation and repair methods for specifications, code, tests, invariants, proofs, and counterexamples while keeping the checker outside the generative model's trusted path.

 - Apply formal methods across the AI-driven software development life cycle, from requirements and architecture through model-generated implementation, continuous integration, release evidence, monitoring, and change-impact analysis.

 - Study composition at system scale, proof and specification maintenance under change, and methods for preserving evidence across tool, model, dependency, and compiler versions.

 - Connect formal artifacts to AIVista's data, rule, action, and process ontologies so runtime decisions can be traced to governing sources, versions, evaluated values, and accepted checks.

 - Define assurance claims with explicit scope, assumptions, trusted components, checker versions, and acceptance boundaries; prevent stronger claims than the evidence supports.

 - Partner with product and engineering teams to transition successful methods into production authoring, verification, and AI-driven software development workflows.

 - Lead publications, patents, open-source contributions, and research partnerships in formal methods, programming languages, software engineering, knowledge representation, and AI-driven software development.

NTT DATA AIVista  |  Formal Methods for AI Driven Software Development Life CyclePage 

Qualifications

Basic

 - PhD in computer science, programming languages, formal methods, software engineering, artificial intelligence, mathematics, or a related field, or equivalent industry impact.

 - At least 5 years of experience in formal methods, software engineering research, artificial intelligence, or machine learning, with significant experience applying research in production environments.

 - A proven record of impactful research demonstrated through publications, patents, open-source tools, formal artifacts, or shipped software products.

 - Deep experience in at least two relevant areas: formal specification, program verification, model checking, theorem proving, static analysis, type systems, program synthesis, requirements engineering, or autoformalization.

 - Hands-on experience building with at least one proof assistant, theorem prover, satisfiability solver, model checker, static analyzer, or verification-aware language.

 - Strong foundations in logic, algorithms, semantics, software architecture, and experimental design, with the ability to state exactly what a check proves and assumes.

 - Proficiency in Python and at least one additional production language, with experience building research prototypes and developer tools that engineering teams can maintain.

Preferred

 - Experience with large-language-model autoformalization, neural theorem proving, verifier-guided generation, proof repair, or AI-driven program synthesis and code generation.

 - Experience with controlled natural language, specification mining, domain-specific languages, traceability, or translating requirements into executable artifacts.

 - Experience with ontologies, semantic modeling languages, description logics, graph constraint languages, rule engines, or policy-as-code systems.

 - Experience modeling business processes, distributed systems, protocols, authorization policies, or workflow semantics using temporal logic, state machines, Petri nets, or Business Process Model and Notation.

 - Experience with proof-carrying artifacts, verified compilation, deductive verification, symbolic execution, abstract interpretation, or assume-guarantee reasoning.

 - Experience with property-based testing, fuzzing, metamorphic testing, mutation testing, benchmark construction, or independent checker design.

 - Experience integrating formal evidence into continuous integration and delivery, change management, artifact versioning, provenance, and reproducible builds.

 - Experience applying formal or semantic methods in regulated or high-stakes domains and collaborating with legal, compliance, safety, or domain experts.

Benefits

 - Medical, dental, and vision insurance

 - 401(k) plan

 - Significant company Health Savings Account contribution

 - Paid holidays and flexible paid time off

Compensation

The estimated base salary range for this role is $300,000 to $400,000 USD. The salary for the successful applicant will depend on job-related factors such as education, training, work experience, business needs, and market demands. This range may be modified in the future. Total compensation also includes variable pay in the form of an annual target bonus and other cash incentives, with a combined potential of up to 100% of base salary.
